items.claim: Best resources: official tutorials 01/02/03/06 (~3h)
items.verdict: verified (links 200; v3.8.0 sources read)

items.claim: Triton paper, Tillet et al. MAPL 2019 (45 min)
items.verdict: verified (link 200)

items.claim: GPU MODE lectures 14 (practical Triton) and 29 (Triton internals), YouTube recordings
items.verdict: verified (lectures README: 'Lecture 14: Practitioner's Guide to Triton', 'Lecture 29: Triton Internals')

items.claim: triton-lang/triton releases as the record of what the compiler can do
items.verdict: carried

items.claim: GPU Puzzles and Triton-Puzzles (~3h each)
items.verdict: verified; added that Triton-Puzzles runs on the interpreter (its README)

items.claim: A kernel is a @triton.jit function at the level of a program instance = a CUDA thread block
items.verdict: verified (compiled: one program = one CTA of num_warps x 32 threads)

items.claim: No threads, warps, shared memory or __syncthreads in the source; power-of-2 blocks; compiler decides thread mapping, staging, vectorisation, synchronisation
items.verdict: verified (interpreter: non-power-of-two arange rejected; compiled layouts and passes shown)

items.claim: Softmax example code
items.verdict: replaced by the page's own softmax, interpreter-checked and compiled

items.claim: tl.program_id replaces blockIdx; grid is a Python tuple
items.verdict: verified

items.claim: tl.arange + pointer arithmetic + mask replace per-thread indexing; coalescing falls out of contiguous offsets
items.verdict: refined: contiguous offsets are necessary but not sufficient; vector width also needs the 16-byte divisibility hints and a length that keeps the mask whole (compiled: n = 1,000 gives scalar loads)

items.claim: tl.load/tl.store move blocks between HBM and registers/smem (compiler's choice)
items.verdict: verified (compiled: LDG/STG for the vector add, cp.async LDGSTS into shared memory for the matmul)

items.claim: Block pointers / tl.make_block_ptr and TMA-backed tensor descriptors for 2D tiles
items.verdict: verified for tensor descriptors (compiled: UTMALDG/UTMASTG on sm_90a and sm_100a; interpreter-checked); make_block_ptr not shown (descriptors are the current form)

items.claim: tl.dot is the tensor-core matmul primitive
items.verdict: verified (compiled: mma.sync, wgmma, tcgen05, MFMA per target)

items.claim: Reductions emit the warp shuffles and smem staging you would hand-write
items.verdict: verified (compiled: 14 SHFL.BFLY, STS/LDS, 3 BAR.SYNC on sm_90a)

items.claim: tl.constexpr + @triton.autotune over block sizes, num_warps, num_stages replace hand-tuning
items.verdict: verified (autotuner.py read)

items.claim: What you give up: warp-level control, explicit smem layouts, fine-grained async, non-power-of-2 blocks
items.verdict: carried; refined: Triton 3.8 exposes some (tensor descriptors, warp_specialize in tl.range); Gluon gives the rest
items.where: Reading in one screen table, s5, s10

items.claim: For roughly 90% of ML kernels the trade is free
items.verdict: unconfirmed opinion; dropped

items.claim: Within 0-20% of expert CUDA in ~10x fewer lines
items.verdict: unconfirmed (no source found); stated as such

items.claim: Portable to AMD; first-class ROCm and Intel XPU backends; kernel layer of PyTorch on all three
items.verdict: AMD verified by compiling for gfx942 and gfx950 from the standard wheel; Intel is a separate repository (intel-xpu-backend-for-triton), not compiled here

items.claim: torch.compile first: it auto-generates Triton for fusions
items.verdict: verified (real Inductor output: one pointwise kernel, one persistent-reduction kernel)

items.claim: torch.compile's matmul/attention templates plus autotuning cover most standard patterns
items.verdict: corrected: Triton matmul templates are used only under max-autotune / max_autotune_gemm (torch/_inductor/utils.py use_triton_template); by default matmuls go to extern_kernels.mm (shown)

items.claim: Write no kernel until a profile shows a gap
items.verdict: carried

items.claim: Hand-written Triton for custom attention, quantised/mixed GEMMs, fused MoE routing, data-dependent structure
items.verdict: carried

items.claim: torch.library custom ops so compile can see through it
items.verdict: verified (torch.library.triton_op and wrap_triton present in 2.14.1)

items.claim: Raw CUDA/CUTLASS for the last 10-30%: warp specialisation, swizzles, clusters, persistent kernels, device APIs, C++ deployment
items.verdict: carried without the 10-30% figure (unsourced)

items.claim: Rule of thumb: prototype in Triton, drop to CUTLASS/CUDA for kernels that dominate the profile
items.verdict: carried

items.claim: Triton 3.7 current line (3.7.0 May 2026, 3.7.1 Jun 2026)

items.claim: Two releases per PyTorch cycle; ships as the triton wheel bundled with PyTorch

items.claim: Mature support Ampere through Blackwell incl. sm_120 (RTX 5090), AMD CDNA (MI300/MI355), Intel XPU
items.verdict: verified for what compiled here: sm_80, sm_90a, sm_100a, sm_120, gfx942, gfx950; B300 and Intel not compiled

items.claim: OpenAI publicly runs Triton/Gluon on both NVIDIA and AMD
items.verdict: unconfirmed; what is public is gpt-oss's Triton reference implementation (triton_kernels MoE)

items.claim: ROCm backend on ROCm 10.0 (August 2026), AMD's 3.3x inference and 2.4x training uplift

items.claim: Gluon: lower-level, explicitly scheduled dialect exposing layouts, TMEM, async TMA, barriers, warp specialisation
items.verdict: verified (Gluon tutorial 01 quote; module contents checked in 3.8.0: tma, mbarrier, warpgroup_mma, allocate_tensor_memory, tcgen05_mma, warp_specialize; compiled a Gluon kernel: no TTIR stage)

items.claim: Gluon is a CuTe-DSL-shaped escape hatch inside Triton
items.verdict: kept as analogy (CuTe DSL is closer to Gluon than to Triton)

items.claim: NVIDIA contributed a CUDA Tile IR backend so Triton picks up Blackwell features without source changes
items.verdict: corrected: an incubator repository (triton-lang/Triton-to-tile-IR), a separate Triton 3.7 build with ENABLE_TILE=1, validated on B200, documented gaps; not in Triton 3.8.0

items.claim: Triton is effectively the shared DSL target NVIDIA, AMD and Intel optimise for
items.verdict: unconfirmed opinion; dropped
